en: The Triplet of the Wholesome (Kusalattika), The Triplet of the Resultant (Vipākattika)
Dependent on a state that is neither unwholesome nor resultant, a neutral resultant state arises by way of the root condition … one.
Dependent on a state that is neither unwholesome nor resultant, a neutral resultant state arises by way of the root condition … one.
Dependent on a state that is both neither unwholesome nor resultant and neither unwholesome nor resultant, a neutral resultant state arises by way of the root condition … one. (Abbreviated.)
Under the condition of cause (hetu), three; ... pe ... under the condition of non-disappearance (avigata), three.

Conditioned by that which is neither wholesome nor of a nature to produce result (na-kusala na-vipākadhamma-dhamma), a wholesome state of a nature to produce result arises by way of the condition of cause.
Conditioned by that which is neither wholesome nor of a nature to produce result, an unwholesome state of a nature to produce result arises by way of the condition of cause; [there are] two.
Conditioned by a state that is neither unwholesome nor subject to ripening, a state that is unwholesome and subject to ripening arises by way of root condition ... two.

Conditioned by a state that is neither wholesome nor subject to ripening and a state that is neither unwholesome nor subject to ripening, a state that is wholesome and subject to ripening arises by way of root condition ... two. (Abbreviated.
In the case of root [condition], there are six ... pe ... in the case of non-disappearance, there are six.

Dependent on unwholesome states that are neither resultant nor of a nature to produce resultants, there arises a neutral state that is neither resultant nor of a nature to produce resultants by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated.
There are six under root, six under predominance … pe … three under mutuality … pe … three under resultant … pe … six under non-disappearance.
